_doc: PROVIDERS, NOT SERIES. Registering 700 series would be registering 700 things that
can rot. Registering a PROVIDER means registering one catalog and one address shape;
traversal picks the series when a need appears. Adding a national institute that
speaks SDMX is then an entry in this file, not an adapter in the codebase.
STATUS IS ABOUT US, NOT ABOUT THEM. `skipped` means we cannot read that dialect yet.
It is not a verdict on the provider and it is not a blacklist — IMF's data is fine;
we simply have no XML reader. Recording the reason is what makes it fixable later
reporter_independence here is the provider's DEFAULT class and is deliberately the
weaker guess where a provider mixes sources. config/reporter_independence.json still
governs, and an unmapped org still resolves to `unknown` — never to independent.
Probed live 2026-08-03: every url and address below was fetched and read.

un_sdg.name: UN SDG Global Database
un_sdg.independence_note: national reporting to the UN, standardised by the custodian agency. Some series (WHO/UNICEF JMP, UNODC) are custodian-estimated and closer to mixed — the org-level map in reporter_independence.json is where that gets decided.
un_sdg.params_note: area is a UN M49 code; 1 is World. Any country code works, which is the same payload the per-country scorer wants.
un_sdg.address_note: many series carry a further breakdown in `dimensions` (Location RURAL/URBAN/ALLAREA, Sex, Age). Where they do, the address is ambiguous without a `where` filter and the reader will say so rather than pick one.

eurostat.name: Eurostat
eurostat.independence_note: member states report to Eurostat, which standardises. The measured entity supplies the figures.
eurostat.why_it_matters: MONTHLY and QUARTERLY official series. Every anchor in this portfolio is annual, and an annual aggregator cannot fill a monthly slot no matter how many of them are added — this is the only route we have to one.
eurostat.sdmx_note: Eurostat's own SDMX 2.1 endpoint answers 406 to SDMX-JSON, with and without an Accept header (probed 2026-08-03). JSON-stat is the working route, so this provider does NOT use the sdmx reader.

ecb.name: European Central Bank Data Portal
ecb.independence_note: market prices and reference rates — an observation of a market, not a party's account of itself. Its statistical series about member states are a different matter and should be classed per-series.

catalog.verified: HTTP 504 at probe time 2026-08-03 — the DATA endpoint answered fine the same minute, so this is their catalogue service being slow, not a dead provider

oecd.name: OECD Data Explorer
oecd.independence_note: member states report; the OECD standardises. Same aggregator logic as the World Bank.
oecd.address_note: OECD needs dimensionAtObservation=AllDimensions; without it the key form is per-dataflow and answers 422. That is why the sdmx reader handles the flat shape as well as the series-major one.

imf.name: International Monetary Fund
imf.skip_reason: api.imf.org answers SDMX-XML only; the older JSON host dataservices.imf.org does not resolve (probed 2026-08-03). We have no XML reader yet.
imf.skip_is_not_a_blacklist: Nothing is wrong with IMF's data. This records a gap in OUR readers so it can be closed deliberately, rather than IMF quietly never appearing again.
imf.unblocks_if: an SDMX-ML reader is added, or IMF exposes SDMX-JSON

_national_institutes_note: The point of one SDMX reader is that adding a national statistical institute is an
entry here, not code. Prefer institutes publishing English metadata; where the
metadata is in another language, record `language` and set status `skipped` with the
reason — a language we cannot read yet is a gap in us, and must not be recorded as a
defect in them. None are registered yet: the reader is proven against ECB and OECD
first, and claiming coverage we have not tested would be exactly the kind of
diversification-on-paper this pack exists to remove.
